clue.text: Session with a man of millions

definitions.meaning: ... Sessions were the English magistrates' sittings that granted liquor licences
the hero of the novel and film ... Millions, who must spend a fortune

explanation.walkthrough: Brewster Sessions were the yearly licensing courts for pubs in England; Brewster's Millions is a comic novel about a man who must squander a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper-name uses: the licensing court's title and the surname of the millionaire hero in a well-known story.

clue.text: A legendary writer seems to prohibit bacon

parts.note: to bar something is to prohibit it
ham and bacon are both cured pork

explanation.surface: A storyteller of legend seems set on banning bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: R. H. Barham wrote The Ingoldsby Legends, which makes him a 'legendary' writer in a literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Barham wrote the comic verse collection The Ingoldsby Legends, so he is a writer of legends.

clue.text: Outward Bound has drive

parts.note: goods shipped abroad are outward bound, and a national campaign to sell abroad was called a drive

explanation.walkthrough: Outward Bound is printed in italics as the title of a play, but the sense is cargo leaving the country, and post-war Britain ran a famous drive to sell abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold abroad are sent outward from the country, and Britain's postwar campaign to sell them was known by this word plus drive.

clue.text: They get the wind up at the movies

definitions.text: They get the wind up at the movies

parts.words: They get the wind up at the movies
parts.note: 'get the wind up' means become scared, but here reels of film are wound up in the cinema

explanation.definitionFit: Reels of film in a cinema projector are wound round these cylinders, so they are literally wound up.

clue.text: Hook that attracts attention

parts.note: a hook in a dress fastening catches the eye of its partner, and a striking sight is said to catch the eye

explanation.walkthrough: A hook-and-eye fastener has a hook that catches the eye; a showy thing that draws looks is called by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking draws people's gaze, and a hook literally catches the eye of a hook-and-eye fastening.

clue.text: "Curates … On ——, clerical, printless toe" (Brooke)

parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Rupert Brooke's poem about Grantchester vicarage: the missing adjective describes the curates' light-footed step

explanation.surface: A line of Rupert Brooke with one word left blank for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Brooke's The Old Vicarage, Grantchester: 'curates, long dust, will come and go / On ___, clerical, printless toe'. The answer is the word that fills the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank asks for the poet's adjective for a supple, light step that leaves no mark.

clue.text: There's a sense of peace in a relic like this

indicators.note: like this tells the solver to reshape in a relic into a word of the form wanted

explanation.surface: Some old relic seems to carry an air of calm about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenical describes what promotes peace or reconciliation, from Greek eirene, peace.

clue.text: Phony sounds of contempt that go to the head

parts.note: a sham is something fake or phony
'pooh' or 'poo' is a scornful noise

explanation.surface: Fake snorts of scorn seem to be going to someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to the head' suggests drink or pride; here it is hair washes applied to the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hair-washing liquids, which are applied literally to the head.

clue.text: " Is she not pure gold, my -—--- ?" (Browning)

definitions.text: " Is she not pure gold, my -—--- ?" (Browning)

parts.words: " Is she not pure gold, my -—--- ?" (Browning)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Browning's A Toccata of Galuppi's, where a Venetian lover praises the woman he adores

explanation.surface: A line of Robert Browning with the last word left blank for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in Browning's A Toccata of Galuppi's runs 'Is she not pure gold, my ___?'. The answer fills the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank asks for the word Browning's speaker uses for the woman he loves, his lady.

clue.text: Rebukes the playful company when it wanders

parts.note: a company of players, a repertory theatre company, is called a rep
to wander is to rove

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe on tour gets told off for drifting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' here means made up of players, so the company is a theatrical rep.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove someone is to rebuke or scold them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Flowery broken plates

indicators.note: broken crockery is in pieces, so the word plates is smashed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner plates with a floral pattern lie smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Petals are the coloured parts of a bloom, so they are the most flowery thing about it.

clue.text: Insect-breeder with the golden touch

definitions.meaning: an old word for a collector and breeder of butterflies and moths
from the Latin for gold, describing something golden in colour

explanation.walkthrough: The insect sense comes from the golden chrysalis (aurelia) of some butterflies, which also gives the word its sense of golden.
explanation.definitionFit: The lepidopterist's old title and the adjective for a gold colour share one Latin root, aurum, gold.

clue.text: Baptist bird ?

definitions.meaning: Baptists, who immerse converts, were nicknamed for plunging them under water
a small songbird that bobs and walks underwater in streams

explanation.definitionFit: One who immerses believers at baptism was mocked with this name, which is also a stream-dwelling songbird.

clue.text: Emphasizes where to find sleepers

definitions.meaning: stresses a word by drawing a line beneath it
railway sleepers are the beams that lie beneath the rails

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepers' suggests people in bed; railway sleepers are the crossbeams lying under the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking text with a rule beneath stresses it; railway sleepers lie beneath the rails.

clue.text: A ducal son's involved in an offensive way

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of a ducal son's are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A duke's heir has got mixed up in something disgraceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scandalous causes outrage, so it is shocking and offensive to decent feeling.

clue.text: An example of cold war escalation ?

definitions.text: An example of cold war escalation ?

parts.words: An example of cold war escalation ?
parts.note: the Cold War of superpowers is the false lead; a war fought with packed icy missiles grows as they roll

explanation.definitionFit: A packed ball of ice is a missile in a literally cold fight, and it grows as it rolls, which is escalation.

clue.text: One of Kingsley's Heroes in action makes a neat job of it ?

definitions.text: makes a neat job of it

parts.note: Tom, hero of Charles Kingsley's The Water-Babies, is a chimney sweep, so the piece is read as sweep's
up means active or astir, as in up and about

explanation.surface: A Kingsley character, roused to action, finishes a task tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley also wrote a book called The Heroes, a false trail; the hero meant is the boy sweep in The Water-Babies, and 'sweep's up' means the sweep is up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy away dirt with a broom is to finish neatly, leaving the place clean.

clue.text: Professional decoration ?

parts.note: a decoration suggests a medal for professional service, but it is just an adornment

explanation.definitionFit: A decoration that embellishes something is an adornment, the plain sense behind the medal suggestion.

clue.text: The option is timely and cannot be repeated

definitions.text: The option is timely and cannot be repeated

parts.words: The option is timely and cannot be repeated
parts.note: a choice that must be taken at once because the chance will not come round again

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a last-chance offer: act at this moment or lose the opportunity for good.

clue.text: In conclusion a skyer

definitions.meaning: the final outcome or result of a matter
in cricket, a skyer is a hit sent high into the air

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a skyer is a ball hit steeply up into the air, which is a shot upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The final result of events is the outcome, and a cricket stroke hit steeply upward is a shot that goes up.

clue.text: A gate-crasher before he was unlocked

definitions.text: A gate-crasher before he was unlocked

parts.words: A gate-crasher before he was unlocked
parts.note: the biblical strongman carried off the gates of Gaza while his hair was still uncut

explanation.walkthrough: A gate-crasher is an uninvited guest, but this strongman carried off the city gates of Gaza; 'unlocked' means shorn of his locks by Delilah.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's strongman tore away Gaza's gates and lost his strength when Delilah had his hair cut off.

clue.text: Macbeth recommended throwing it to the dogs

definitions.text: Macbeth recommended throwing it to the dogs

parts.words: Macbeth recommended throwing it to the dogs
parts.note: Macbeth tells the doctor to throw his medicine to the dogs, saying he will none of it

explanation.walkthrough: In Act 5 Macbeth says to the doctor 'Throw ___ to the dogs; I'll none of it.'
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for medicine is what Macbeth tells the doctor to toss to the dogs.

clue.text: At the time of Julia's going and taking silk ?

definitions.meaning: an archaic conjunction meaning when or while
Robert Herrick's poem opens with Julia going about dressed in silks

explanation.walkthrough: Herrick's lyric Upon Julia's Clothes begins 'Whenas in silks my Julia goes'. 'Taking silk' also means becoming a senior barrister, a false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means when, and it is the first word of Herrick's famous line about Julia in silks.

clue.text: Blow and ——-- ! How careless can one get !

parts.note: a slap is a blow with the open hand
the blank printed in the clue is a dash

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation, 'Blow and dash!', at someone's sloppy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow and dash!' reads as a mild oath, but the printed blank itself is a dash, the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and careless, done without attention.

clue.text: One was earnestly sought from a female bicyclist

definitions.text: One was earnestly sought from a female bicyclist

parts.words: One was earnestly sought from a female bicyclist
parts.note: the old song Daisy Bell begs Daisy for a reply, promising a bicycle built for two

explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song Daisy Bell goes 'Daisy, Daisy, give me your ___ do', and the singer pictures her on a tandem bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer is pleading for a reply to his proposal from Daisy, pictured riding a tandem bicycle.

clue.text: His son shouldered him out of Troy

definitions.text: His son shouldered him out of Troy

parts.words: His son shouldered him out of Troy
parts.note: in the Aeneid, Aeneas carries his elderly father on his back from the burning city

explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's hero Aeneas bore his aged father on his shoulders as Troy fell, so the clue names the father.

clue.text: Home of high-flying flappers

parts.note: the floating island in Gulliver's Travels, where servants called flappers tap dreamy masters to rouse them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flappers' suggests 1920s young women; in Swift, flappers carry bladders to flap their absent-minded masters into attention, on an island that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's flying island in Gulliver's Travels is where the flappers serve, so it is literally their high-flying home.

clue.text: Is love the bracer needed to get the same tone ?

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
a bracer is a reviving drink, a tonic

explanation.surface: Asking whether love is the pick-me-up needed to restore one's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotonic means having equal tension or tone, from Greek for equal plus tone.
